themes.title: US AI czar: 120-day risk report
themes.summary: Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as AI czar, and the White House task force he leads will deliver a report on AI risks and the federal government's responsibility within 120 days. Clayton has begun unveiling the task force's goals and membership, recasting AI oversight as a national-security matter.
themes.angle: AI policy is now intelligence policy — the 120-day clock gives boards a concrete compliance horizon.

themes.title: Rogue agents rewrite liability
themes.summary: Axios reports AI agents are automating known hacking techniques at machine speed, overwhelming the internet's defenses, while The Information and NYT both flag the accountability vacuum: who is legally responsible when an agent goes rogue? Expect novel legal battles as agent deployments scale.
themes.angle: Agentic AI is becoming a liability and cyber-risk question — boards need agent governance before the first D&O claim.

themes.title: GCC enterprise AI: US pact, Arabic models, ADGM
themes.summary: The UAE-US technology partnership — reported at $1.4tn and spanning AI, space and quantum — advanced through high-level Washington engagements (Arabian Business, UAE Embassy). Regionally: a Saudi dataset is cutting Arabic-dialect AI errors, Riyadh and Abu Dhabi host AI summits, and Coinbase won an ADGM licence for a tokenised-securities hub.
themes.angle: GCC AI is moving from compute buildout to capability depth — Arabic model quality and regulated fintech rails are the next battlegrounds.

themes.title: AI safety: exits, alarms, pushback
themes.summary: The safety debate escalated on multiple fronts: an OpenAI safety employee quit calling for nuclear-level safeguards (Bloomberg), Treasury Secretary Bessent branded existential warnings alarmist and demanded the industry police itself, and Axios reports Altman's veiled clash with Anthropic over attributing religious power to models.
themes.angle: Safety exits and regulatory pushback are two sides of the same governance vacuum — watch who leaves and who gets hired next.

themes.title: Compute economics: talent, futures, on-device
themes.summary: Anthropic is spending $100m to train 10,000 engineers on enterprise AI; FT reports chip-rental price swings are creating a futures market in compute; a16z backs Conway's on-device model Underdog (corroborated by Sigil Wen's private-AI launch); McKinsey argues agentic AI forces a pause-pivot-accelerate choice for SaaS and that CEO ownership decides AI outcomes.
themes.angle: Inference economics is becoming a tradable market — CFOs should track compute volatility like a commodity input.
